newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience shares up amid partnership talk.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience shares up amid partnership talk.

text.p: Speculation that biotech specialist Chiroscience Group Plc may be preparing to announce a drug development agreement with a major drug company helped boost its shares in morning trading on Thursday.
Shares in Cambridge-based Chiroscience were up 17 pence at 385 pence at 1010 GMT after touching a high of 395 pence.
Analysts have been expecting Chiroscience to announce a partnership on at least one of its major projects to develop novel drugs for cancer, asthma and arthritis.
The company is developing drugs for the treatment of cancer and arthritis which are similar in action to British Biotech Plc's potentially ground-breaking cancer drug Marimastat.

One analyst, who asked not to be named, said that with Marimastat looking increasingly likely to succeed, major drug companies may be interested in linking up with Chiroscience's less advanced version.
"People don't want to wait for Phase III (results) on Marimastat to do something. They want to get involved now," he said. "A lot of peple could be interested in doing a deal with Chiroscience."
The analyst said, however, he believes a partnership on Chiroscience's arthritis compound D5140, which is more advanced than its cancer project, is the most likely to be announced in the near term.
